# HIPAA Security Rule (45 CFR Part 164, Subparts C & E): scanner coverage map

<!-- generated by scripts/compliance-coverage.mjs from the framework file; do not edit by hand -->

This page lists every control the scanner evaluates for HIPAA Security Rule (45 CFR Part 164, Subparts C & E), taken from `scanner/src/posture/compliance-frameworks/hipaa-security-rule.json`, the file the engine reads. It is regenerated from that file and checked for staleness, so it cannot disagree with what is assessed.

```bash
/compliance --walkthrough hipaa-security-rule
/compliance --report hipaa-security-rule
```

**8 controls** are evaluated: 6 with an automated mapping, 2 needing a person to attest. By how much a code scan can observe: 4 yes, 3 partial, 1 no.

**Scope.** SELECTIVE SUBSET. 8 of the Security Rule technical safeguards. Administrative and physical safeguards are outside what a code scanner can observe and are NOT represented here.

| Control | Requirement | Observable in code | Evaluated from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `§164.308(a)(1)` | Security management process — risk analysis and risk management. | partial | `module:scan-history`, `module:triage` |
| `§164.308(a)(3)` | Workforce security — authorization and supervision of access. | yes | `family:auth-missing`, `family:iam-overpermissive` |
| `§164.308(a)(4)` | Information access management — minimum necessary access. | yes | `family:idor`, `family:authz`, `family:k8s-rbac-cluster-admin` |
| `§164.308(a)(5)` | Security awareness and training. | no | a person attests |
| `§164.312(a)(1)` | Technical safeguards — access control (unique user identification, automatic logoff, encryption/decryption). | yes | `family:hardcoded-secret`, `family:crypto-weak-cipher` |
| `§164.312(b)` | Audit controls — record and examine activity in systems containing PHI. | partial | `module:fix-history` |
| `§164.312(c)` | Integrity — PHI not altered or destroyed in an unauthorized manner. | partial | a person attests |
| `§164.312(e)` | Transmission security — PHI in transit is protected. | yes | `family:crypto-tls-no-verify`, `family:crypto-tls-version`, `graph:transit-protection:PHI:external:transit:protected` |

## What this does not do

<!-- limits-verified: 2026-10-20 -->

- **It is a subset.** Only the controls above are evaluated. Everything else in the framework is outside what a code scan can observe and is not assessed here.
- **It is evidence, not an assessment.** A control reported as present means the mapped signals are clean on the last scan. It is not an attestation, a certification or a statement of compliance.
- **A control needing attestation is not evidenced.** Those controls are listed so the gap is visible, and they stay open until a person attests.
